extracted.intended_audience: recipients of Federal financial assistance (IHEs, LEAs, other recipients), institutional compliance officers, legal counsel, and stakeholders responding to the Title IX final rule
extracted.subtask_description: Final regulations and preamble for 34 CFR part 106 (Title IX) setting purpose, definitions, regulatory analyses (accounting statement, RFA, PRA), recordkeeping/ICR requirements, small-entity size standards, and related procedural/regulatory requirements for recipients of Federal education funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accounting statement (OMB Circular A-4)
rubrics_metrics.description: As required by OMB Circular A-4, the Department's accounting statement shows the classification of the expenditures associated with the provisions of the final regulations, with estimated costs of $98,505,145 in the first year and $12,038,087 in cost savings in subsequent years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides Department's best estimate of changes in annualized monetized costs, benefits, and transfers resulting from the final regulations; used to inform rulemaking cost–benefit considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discount rates used in accounting
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department calculates monetized impacts using discount rates of 3% and 7%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both discount rates are presented in the accounting table to show monetized results under alternative discounting assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimated annualized costs and benefits by category
rubrics_metrics.description: Categories include: Reading and Understanding the Regulations; Policy Revisions; Publishing Notice of Nondiscrimination; Training of Title IX Coordinators; Updating Training Materials; Supportive Measures; Group A Investigations; Group B Investigations; Appeal Process; Informal Resolutions; Creation and Maintenance of Documentation; with numeric estimates shown for 3% and 7% discount rates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table lists per-category dollar estimates (e.g., Supportive Measures $9,142,455; Group B Investigations negative ($63,650,843); Appeal Process $17,776,304; totals vary by discount rate). These line items inform the overall accounting statement and RIA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Flexibility Act (RFA) – certification and FRFA requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If an agency cannot certify that a final rule will not have a significant economic impact on a substantial number of small entities, it must prepare a Final Regulatory Flexibility Analysis (FRFA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FRFA must identify number of small entities affected, assess economic impact on those small entities, and consider less burdensome alternatives that meet regulatory objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'small IHE' (enrollment-based size standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: For this rulemaking, the Department defines 'small IHE' as (1) a less-than-two-year IHE with enrollment of fewer than 750 students, or (2) an at-least-two-year-but-less-than-four-year IHE, or a four-year institution, with enrollment of fewer than 1,000 students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department chose enrollment-based thresholds (rather than SBA revenue-based standards) to allow meaningful comparisons across for-profit, non-profit, and public IHEs; justification and comparison to prior standards and SBA discussed in preamble.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rationale for enrollment-based small-entity standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Enrollment is correlated with revenue and resources; enrollment data are more readily available and allow consistent cross-sector comparison; NAICS/revenue thresholds vary by program type and are difficult to align.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department consulted SBA Office of Advocacy and reports ~93% agreement between the revised enrollment standard and SBA revenue standard for proprietary IHEs; enrollment-based approach captures similar universe of small entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empirical count of small IHEs under enrollment definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Table presenting number of small vs. not small IHEs by sector: total 6,003 IHEs, with 3,635 classified as small under the enrollment-based definition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Source: 2022 IPEDS data reported to the Department; used to estimate affected population and aggregate impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'small LEA'
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department defines 'small LEA' as either (1) a traditional public school district located in a county with total population under 50,000, or (2) a charter school LEA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: charter LEAs' average size and geographic limitations make dominance unlikely; this approach proxies SBA's small government entity definition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimated projected burden on small IHEs (monetized and percent of revenue)
rubrics_metrics.description: Based on the model: a Group A IHE will see a net increase of approximately $8,477 per year; using average revenues, the Department estimates this to be approximately 0.10% of annual revenue for small IHEs; ~684 IHEs with revenues < $847,700 could see costs exceed 1% of revenues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimates assume small IHEs conduct same number of investigations per year as average; Department notes actual number likely lower, so realized costs may be less.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimated projected burden on small LEAs
rubrics_metrics.description: An LEA in Group A will see a net increase of approximately $2,623 per year; using average small LEA revenues, estimated gross costs are approximately 0.02% of total annual revenues; ~117 small LEAs with very low revenues could see costs exceed 1%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assumes small LEAs conduct same number of investigations per year as average; smaller LEAs likely conduct fewer investigations, so estimates probably overstate actual burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimated projected burden on other small recipients
rubrics_metrics.description: Other recipients in Group A will see a net increase of approximately $3,754 per year; at assumed average annual revenue of $3,500,000, estimated cost is ~0.08% of revenues; costs would exceed 1% only for recipients with annual revenues under ~$375,400.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department lacks comprehensive revenue data for other recipients; uses distributional assumptions and Department grant data to justify conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussion of significant alternatives for small entities
rubrics_metrics.description: Alternatives considered: (1) extend effective date for small entities; (2) waive certain requirements for small entities; (3) propose different requirements for smaller recipients. All were rejected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasons for rejection: extending effective date would delay enforcement of Title IX rights; waivers or different requirements would jeopardize civil rights protections and are inconsistent with Title IX's nondiscrimination mandate; final regulations are adaptable to various settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paperwork Reduction Act (PRA) public comment and purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: Under PRA, the Department must provide the public and Federal agencies an opportunity to comment on proposed and continuing collections to ensure clarity, minimize burden, and properly assess impact of collection requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PRA goals include ensuring public understands collection instructions, format, minimizing reporting burden, and accurate assessment of impact on respondents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping burden estimates (Year 1 and ongoing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Year 1 additional recordkeeping burden: 4 hours per LEA, 16 hours per IHE, 4 hours per other recipient; total Year 1 net increase of 171,024 hours. Ongoing annual burden: 2 hours per LEA, 6 hours per IHE, 2 hours per other recipient; total ongoing annual increase 73,506 hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department believes §106.8(f) will not change disclosure requirements for three reasons: prior obligations under 2020 amendments, anecdotal evidence of existing practices for alternative disciplinary proceedings and sex discrimination records, and thus many recipients will experience de minimis increases in disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information Collection Request (ICR) and OMB control number
rubrics_metrics.description: Collection identified as proposed OMB control number 1870-0505; changes will increase burden over first seven years by $44,448,753 and 612,060 hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ICR prepared to capture recordkeeping and information collection impacts associated with final §106.8(f); figures used in PRA compliance and OMB review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of educational impact / interagency information transmission
rubrics_metrics.description: Final regulations do not require transmission of information that any other agency or authority of the United States gathers or makes available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department requested comments on this point in the July 2022 NPRM and reviewed responses in making this determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federalism consultation requirement (EO 13132)
rubrics_metrics.description: Executive Order 13132 requires meaningful and timely input by State and local elected officials on policies with federalism implications; Department identified potential federalism-implicative sections in NPRM and solicited comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preamble discusses comments received from state and local officials concerning potential federalism implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessible format availability
rubrics_metrics.description: On request, individuals with disabilities can obtain the document in accessible formats (e.g., RTF, txt, thumb drive, MP3, braille, large print, audiotape, CD, or other accessible format).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests should be made to the program contact listed under FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT; Department will provide appropriate accessible formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic access to Federal Register and CFR documents
rubrics_metrics.description: The official edition is available at www.govinfo.gov and documents published by the Department in the Federal Register are available at www.federalregister.gov (article search/advanced search).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PDF access requires Adobe Acrobat Reader; advanced search can limit to Department documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority citation for part 106
rubrics_metrics.description: Authority: 20 U.S.C. 1681 et seq., unless otherwise noted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory authority grounds the regulatory provisions in this part.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of part 106 (§106.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Purpose is to effectuate Title IX—to eliminate (with certain exceptions) discrimination on basis of sex in any education program or activity receiving Federal financial assistance—and to effectuate section 844 of the Education Amendments of 1974.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serves as the regulatory statement of objectives and scope for part 106.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Administrative law judge
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative law judge means a person appointed by the reviewing authority to preside over a hearing held under §106.81.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Administratively separate unit
rubrics_metrics.description: Administratively separate unit means a school, department, or college of an educational institution (other than a local educational agency), admission to which is independent of admission to any other component of such institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Admission
rubrics_metrics.description: Admission means selection for part-time, full-time, special, associate, transfer, exchange, or any other enrollment, membership, or matriculation in or at an education program or activity operated by a recipient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant, as used in the definition of educational institution and in §106.4, means one who submits an application, request, or plan required to be approved by a Department official, or by a recipient, as a condition to becoming a recipient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Assistant Secretary
rubrics_metrics.description: Assistant Secretary means the Assistant Secretary for Civil Rights of the Department.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Complainant
rubrics_metrics.description: Complainant means: (1) A student or employee who is alleged to have been subjected to conduct that could constitute sex discrimination under Title IX or this part; or (2) A person other than a student or employee who is alleged to have been subjected to conduct that could constitute sex discrimination under Title IX or this part and who was participating or attempting to participate in the recipient's education program or activity at the time of the alleged sex discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies who may serve as a complainant for purposes of Title IX investigations and procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Complaint
rubrics_metrics.description: Complaint means an oral or written request to the recipient that objectively can be understood as a request for the recipient to investigate and make a determination about alleged discrimination under Title IX or this part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes objective understanding of a request as a trigger for investigation obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Confidential employee
rubrics_metrics.description: Confidential employee means: (1) An employee whose communications are privileged or confidential under Federal or State law (only with respect to information received while functioning within scope of those duties); (2) an employee designated as confidential under this part for providing services related to sex discrimination (confidentiality only applies to information received in connection with providing those services); or (3) a postsecondary institution employee conducting an IRB‑approved human-subjects research study on sex discrimination (status only with respect to information received while conducting the study).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limits confidentiality to specific contexts and duties; distinguishes institutional designations and legal privileges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Department
rubrics_metrics.description: Department means the Department of Education.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Disciplinary sanctions
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary sanctions means consequences imposed on a respondent following a determination under Title IX that the respondent violated the recipient's prohibition on sex discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Educational institution
rubrics_metrics.description: Educational institution means a local educational agency (as defined in ESEA), a preschool, a private elementary or secondary school, or an applicant or recipient that is an institution of graduate higher education, undergraduate higher education, professional education, or vocational education.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Elementary school
rubrics_metrics.description: Elementary school means elementary school as defined by ESEA and a public or private preschool.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Federal financial assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal financial assistance means: (1) grants or loans (including funds for building, scholarships, wages, etc.); (2) grants of Federal real or personal property or proceeds of sale if Federal share not properly accounted for; (3) provision of services of Federal personnel; (4) sale or lease of Federal property at nominal or reduced consideration or permission to use Federal property without consideration; (5) any other contract/agreement/arrangement with purpose of providing assistance to any education program or activity (except insurance or guaranty contracts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerates the types of federal assistance that trigger Title IX obligations for recipients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Institution of graduate higher education
rubrics_metrics.description: Means an institution offering academic study beyond the bachelor's degree or awards degrees beyond the first professional degree, or awards no degree but ordinarily facilitates research by persons with highest graduate degrees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Institution of professional education
rubrics_metrics.description: Means an institution (except any institution of undergraduate higher education) offering a program leading to a first professional degree in a field with a national specialized accrediting agency recognized by the Secretary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Institution of undergraduate higher education
rubrics_metrics.description: Means an institution offering at least two but less than four years of college-level study leading to a diploma or associate degree, or offering academic study leading to a baccalaureate degree, or an agency/body that certifies credentials or offers degrees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Institution of vocational education
rubrics_metrics.description: Means a school/institution (except professional/graduate/undergraduate institutions) whose primary purpose is to prepare students for technical, skilled, or semiskilled occupations or technical study, whether or not it offers certificates/diplomas/degrees and whether or not it offers full-time study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Parental status
rubrics_metrics.description: Parental status, as used in specified sections, means the status of a person who is: (1) a biological parent; (2) an adoptive parent; (3) a foster parent; (4) a stepparent; (5) a legal custodian or guardian; (6) in loco parentis with respect to such a person; or (7) actively seeking legal custody, guardianship, visitation, or adoption of such a person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies roles covered by 'parental status' for purposes of provisions referenced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Party
rubrics_metrics.description: Party means a complainant or respondent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Peer retaliation
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer retaliation means retaliation by a student against another student.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Postsecondary institution
rubrics_metrics.description: Means an institution of graduate higher education, undergraduate higher education, professional education, or vocational education that serves postsecondary students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Pregnancy or related conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Means: (1) pregnancy, childbirth, termination of pregnancy, or lactation; (2) medical conditions related to pregnancy, childbirth, termination of pregnancy, or lactation; (3) recovery from pregnancy, childbirth, termination of pregnancy, lactation, or related medical conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to clarify recipients' responsibilities toward students and employees based on pregnancy or related conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Program or activity / program
rubrics_metrics.description: Program or activity and program means all operations of: (1)(i) a department, agency, special purpose district, or other instrumentality of State/local government; or (ii) the entity of a State/local government that distributes such assistance; (2)(i) a college, university, or other postsecondary institution, or public system of higher education; or (ii) a local educational agency, system of vocational education, or other school system; (3)(i) an entire corporation/partnership/private organization/sole proprietorship if assistance is extended to it as a whole or if principally engaged in providing education, health care, housing, social services, or parks/recreation; or (ii) the entire plant or comparable facility to which assistance is extended; (4) any other entity established by two or more entities described in paragraphs (1)-(3) any part of which is extended Federal financial assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines the scope of operations and entities covered by Title IX when Federal financial assistance is involved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Recipient
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipient means any State or political subdivision, instrumentality, public or private agency, institution, organization, or other entity, or any person, to whom Federal financial assistance is extended directly or through another recipient and which operates an education program or activity receiving such assistance, including any subunit, successor, assignee, or transferee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broadly identifies who is bound by Title IX regulatory obligations when receiving Federal assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Relevant (evidence/questions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Relevant means related to the allegations of sex discrimination under investigation as part of grievance procedures under §106.45, and if applicable §106.46; questions are relevant when they seek evidence that may aid in showing whether the alleged sex discrimination occurred, and evidence is relevant when it may aid a decisionmaker in determining whether the alleged sex discrimination occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets the evidentiary relevance standard for investigation questioning and decisionmaking under the grievance procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: Remedies means measures provided, as appropriate, to a complainant or any other person the recipient identifies as having had their equal access limited or denied by sex discrimination; measures provided to restore or preserve that person's access to the recipient's education program or activity after a recipient determines sex discrimination occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes the intended effect and target of remedies following a determination of sex discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Respondent
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent means a person who is alleged to have violated the recipient's prohibition on sex discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Retaliation
rubrics_metrics.description: Retaliation means intimidation, threats, coercion, or discrimination against any person by the recipient, a student, an employee, or other person authorized by the recipient to provide aid/benefit/service under the recipient's education program or activity, for the purpose of interfering with any right or privilege secured by Title IX or this part, or because the person has reported information, made a complaint, testified, assisted, or participated or refused to participate in any manner in an investigation, proceeding, or hearing under this part (including informal resolution, grievance procedures, and other actions under §106.44(f)(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to retaliation arising from participation in any Title IX-related process (investigations, hearings, informal resolution, or other actions).
